correctness.rationale: For odd prime p, N>=5 in characteristic zero, gradient dependence of F=sum x_i^(p+1) on the hyperplane sum x_i=0 forces all x_i^p equal to a nonzero scalar. Projective rescaling gives a p-th-root word. Vanishing sum of its coordinates means the integer polynomial sum n_j T^j (deg<p) is a multiple of irreducible Phi_p, hence all n_j=m and N=pm. Projective scaling by a common root acts freely, yielding (pm)!/[p(m!)^p] geometric singular points and none otherwise. On x_N=1 eliminating x_{N-1}, the Hessian is c*(diag(y_i^-1)+w^-1 11^T) with determinant -c^(N-2) w^-1 prod y_i^-1 !=0, hence ordinary double points and reduced Jacobian scheme. Isolated singularities for a hypersurface of dimension N-3>=2 imply geometric integrality and Serre S2,R1 normality. Every balanced word uses all p roots and coordinate ratios generate Q(zeta_p); Galois acts freely with degree p-1, so the finite etale scheme splits into B=A/(p-1) copies. Coordinate permutations give stabilizers (S_m)^p semidirect C_p for geometric points and AGL1(Fp) for closed orbits; standard cyclotomic Frobenius residue degree ord_p(ell) yields the finite-etale spread point count. Independent exact balanced-word counts p=3,m=2 => 30 nodes,15 closed; p=5,m=1 =>24 nodes,6 closed. Not a test of every p,N.

evidence: Minimal polynomial Phi_p implies balanced coordinates, but does not imply that the affine restricted Hessian is nondegenerate, scheme is reduced, and all closed points have degree p-1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Those steps are independently proved by explicit determinant lemma and coordinate-ratio field argument. Special p,N cases are not claimed novel merely by having numerical node totals.
